quote.text: Most adults have had a number of really bad moments, and of course not even failry happy people manage to be happy the whole darn time.
It's so hard to find the words when all you really want to say is: "I can see you're hurting."

Becasue that was a parents job: to provide shoulders. Shoulders for your children to sit on when they're little so they can see the world, then stand on when they get older so they can reach the clouds, and sometimes lean aganst whenever they stumble and feel unsure.
She hoped they were, because sometimes it's easier to live with your own anxieties if you know that no one else is happy, eihter.
Because the terrible thing about becoming an adult is being forced to realize that absolutely nobody care about us, we have to deal with everything ourselves now, find out how the whole world works.
Life doesn't turn out the way you expect.
Life can go all sorts of different ways, but it will probably go wrong.

Even astonishingly late in life, people seem incapable of considering that their parents might not be super-smart and really funny and immortal. Perhaps there's a biological reason for that, that up to a certain age a child loves you unconditionally and hopelessly for one single reason: you're theirs. Which is a pretty smart move on biology's part, you have to give it that.

That's the sort of thing you never really notice until you belong to someone else, the fact that those of us give children their names are the least willing to use them. We give those we love nicknames, because love requires a word that belongs to us alone.

When you are infatuated you can't think about anything else, you forget about your friends, your work, your lunch. If we were infatuated all the tiime we'd have starve to death. And being in love means being infatuated ... from time to time. You have to be sensible. The problem is that everything is relative, happiness is based on expectations, and we have the Internet now. A whole world constatly asking us: "But is your life as perfect as this? Well? How about now? Is it as perfect as this? If it isn't, change it!"
